title: Syndication Onboarding & Handoff Playbook — Scrapbook
content:
Purpose
This is a working playbook/scrapbook intended to speed up partner syndication and marketplace listing handoffs. Mix of copy snippets, acceptance checkpoints, technical gating notes, and communication templates. Goal: reduce back-and-forth and give CS/PM/Eng a one-page scavenger map for a push to a channel (AWS Marketplace, Azure Marketplace, GCP Partner Gallery or cloud vendor syndication).

Summary (one line)
Minimum set of copy assets + tech acceptance checklist + rollout handoff template to move a listing from 'partner-ready' to 'published' in a single sprint.

High-level steps (proposed)
1) Partner kickoff + intent doc (owner: Partner Manager) — collect legal SKU intent, pricing model, and compliance needs.
2) Copy sprint (owner: Content) — generate tile + short description + 1-liner + 3 bullets + trial CTA variations.
3) Tech acceptance (owner: Solutions Eng) — run checklist below against Dedicated/Hosted/Private variants.
4) Packaging + SKU mapping (owner: Finance ops) — map internal SKUs to marketplace meter IDs.
5) Preflight QA (owner: Release Eng) — run acceptance tests and dry publish in vendor sandbox.
6) Publish + Monitor (owner: GTM ops) — notify support, check observability dashboards for errors/latency/cost spikes.

Copy Snippets (wireframe versions for rapid A/B)
- Tile headline (short): Redwood Inference — Predictable, low-latency LLM inference (hosted & private)
- 1-liner (30–60 chars): Production-grade LLM inference for apps that need reliability and throughput.
- Short description (250 chars): Redwood Inference delivers a unified runtime to serve text generation, embeddings, and chat across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Control latency, cost, and compliance with autoscaling, KV caching, and rollout policies.
- 3 bullets (benefits):
  • Unified API for hosted, reserved, and private inference
  • SLA-backed throughput and predictable unit economics
  • Built-in observability and regression-safe rollouts
- Trial CTA variants: Start free trial; Request dedicated demo; Contact sales for private deployment

Alternate messaging (enterprise tone)
- Headline: Enterprise LLM inference — predictable performance, private control
- 1-liner: Deploy with VPC and KMS integrations for regulated workloads.

Guidelines for marketplace copy (vendor-specific notes)
- AWS: emphasize metering model, AMI/dedicated SKU differences, and required security artifacts (CIS, SOC doc pointers). Avoid using the word "free" for metered trials; prefer "trial credit".
- Azure: call out Azure AD SSO and managed identity support; include ARM template notes if private deployment offered.
- GCP: provide region compatibility info (us-west, europe-west), and GCP-specific billing SKU mapping.

Technical Acceptance Checklist (must pass all items before preflight)
- Authentication: API key + role-based access clarity, and vendor SSO mapping documented.
- Model variants: confirm model images/containers for each supported SKU (full model name + version).
- Networking: egress/ingress rules and VPC peering instructions included.
- Data handling: clear statement on ephemeral vs. persistent logs, whether customer prompts are stored, and KMS/HSM integration for keys.
- Metrics: token-level cost counters exposed, per-route latency metrics available in console.
- Billing hooks: webhook URL + sample payload for invoice reconciliation verified in sandbox.
- Failure modes: documented fallback model mapping and rate-limit behavior.
- Compliance artifacts: SOC2 summary, data residency options, encryption at rest/in transit.
- Scalability test: minimum throughput demonstration (tokens/s) and latency p95 under expected load.

Acceptance Test Cases (quick list)
- Smoke: create API key -> call text generation -> stream finish
- Scale: synthetic load at X concurrent clients -> assert p95 latency < target and no OOMs
- Failover: kill primary model process -> requests route to fallback variant within policy window
- Billing: trigger usage event -> assert webhook payload sent and contains expected fields

SKU & Packaging Notes (example template to fill)
- Internal sku_id: RINF-MKT-STD-001
- Marketplace meter id: <to be filled by vendor>
- Offer type: metered / per-token / subscription
- Trial policy: 14-day trial credit or 0–$ credit note

Preflight Runbook (publish day checklist)
- Create sandbox listing and push draft copy
- Run smoke tests across 3 regions (us-west, eu-west, ap-south)
- Validate price display and trial CTA behavior
- Run legal checklist: T&C link, privacy link, support SLA link
- Notify Customer Success and Support with release notes and sample troubleshooting steps

Communication templates (short)
- Slack (to #marketplace-ops): "[PUSH] Sandbox draft for <partner> pushed — requesting QA run. KS: @miguel @luca — acceptance checklist attached: <confluence link>"
- Email to partner: "We pushed the draft listing to vendor sandbox. Please review the tile copy, pricing display, and trial CTA. Reply with approval or edits by EOD Thursday."

Common Gotchas (lessons from previous launches)
- Vendor portals rewrite copy to fit templates; keep tile headlines flexible and avoid long product names.
- Metering mismatch: vendor meter ID assigned late — block until reconciled or risk incorrect billing.
- Private deployment options often require a separate offer entry (not just an add-on).
- Document rollback play for post-publish incidents (who rotates keys, who disables offers).

Open questions / TODOs
- Determine canonical support flow for marketplace-originated tickets (automated vs manual routing).
- Create a small template for compliance artifacts (SOC2 one-pager) that vendor UI accepts (pdf size limits).
- Align with Finance on SKU naming convention for reseller channels (done: proposal v0 above, needs sign-off).
- Draft an automation script that validates tile copy length and screenshots for vendor constraints.

Artifacts to attach before handoff
- Approved copy doc (this file counts as working draft)
- Technical runbook + test harness links
- Compliance package (SOC2 summary, penetration test report)
- Pricing spreadsheet with SKU mapping and billing webhook example

Quick checklist for go/no-go (single line checks)
- [ ] Copy approved by partner and content
- [ ] Tech acceptance checklist all green
- [ ] SKU mapping completed
- [ ] Sandbox tests passed in at least 2 regions
- [ ] Support playbook published and stakeholders notified

Notes to self (scrapbook fragments)
- Try microcopy variant: "Start inference in minutes" vs "Start your trial" — which converts better? run A/B.
- Keep 1-liner under 55 characters for tile preview (some portals truncate aggressively).
- Use neutral screenshots for tile (no PII) — show console latency graph and API example.

Version history
- v0.1 2024-11-20: initial draft, copy + checklist + rough templates (Jaya)
- v0.2 2024-12-02: added acceptance tests and vendor-specific notes (Miguel)

If you pull from this doc for a partner push, please:
- Create a new child doc with final copy + filled SKU mapping and tag the doc with the vendor name.
- Drop a link to that child doc in #marketplace-ops and ping the release eng on duty.

End of playbook — working draft.
